Description:
A pointed cone made by revolving a planar profile 360 degrees around the z axis, standing not on a flat
base but on a second, inward pointing cone.
The profile is a triangle in the x/z plane, x = radius r, y = height z:
  A = (0, 24)    apex of the outer cone, ON the axis
  B = (10, 0)    outer rim of the base
  C = (0, 7.5)   apex of the inward cone, ON the axis
closed by the segment C -> A, which lies ON the axis of revolution and therefore sweeps nothing.
That is the point of the case: a revolve whose profile meets the axis twice, so the result is made of two
conical faces only - a pole at each apex, one shared base circle, and no planar face anywhere. The body
stands on a circle, not on a face.
Dimensions do not matter here, only the shape: base radius R = 10, height H = 24, depth of the recess
d = 7.5, chosen so both slant lengths are integral (26 and 12.5).
Expected:
One closed, consistent solid of two conical faces meeting in the base circle r = 10 at z = 0, with a pole
at (0,0,24) and a pole at (0,0,7.5). A full revolve splits each of the two faces at the seam, so four
ConicalSurface faces are the expected record, not a defect.
All values are exact, computed not measured:
  volume      outer cone minus recess cone = 1/3*pi*R^2*(H-d) = 550*pi = 1727.8759594744
  area        the two lateral surfaces, there is no base face:
              slant outer  sqrt(10^2 + 24^2)  = 26
              slant recess sqrt(10^2 + 7.5^2) = 12.5
              pi*R*(26 + 12.5) = 385*pi = 1209.5132339605
  edgeLength  base circle 2*pi*10 = 62.8318530718, plus the seam of each face:
              2*26 + 2*12.5 = 77, total 139.8318530718
  extent      -10, -10, 0, 10, 10, 24
  consistent  true

spike.verified: 2026-08-26 GH: matches the hand computed values - volume 550*pi = 1727.8759594744 to 2.1e-7 and area 385*pi = 1209.5131716321 to 2e-12, edgeLength 139.8318530718 exactly. Two conical faces split at the seam into four, a pole at each apex, no planar face. The area was 1209.5132339605 (5.6e-4 off) while it was summed over the flat triangles; since ShellMetrics integrates |Su x Sv| over the parameter domain it is exact here, because the domain of a cone mantle is a rectangle and needs no mesh at all.

STILL OPEN, and this case is slow because of it: triangulating a face with a pole does not converge.
Call id 4 asks for precision 1e-5, which reaches Face.GetSimpleTriangulation as maxDeflection 5e-5, and
a single half cone then produces about 39000 triangles from 20000 vertices - the hard cap
maxVerts = max(20000, inputVertexCount*50) in CDTriangulation.Refine. It stops at the cap, it does not
converge. Measured on the same face, boundary sampled with 30 points:
    maxDeflection 0.32     118 triangles   area 406.6865   (true 408.4070)
    maxDeflection 0.05   37368 triangles   area 409.6935   18303 of the Steiner points from the shape
                                                           quality criterion
    maxDeflection 0.05     680 triangles   area 413.7600   same, with MinAngle3D set to 0
    maxDeflection 5e-5   39114 triangles   area 405.0733   19538 Steiner points from edge deflection,
                                                           quality plays no part, the cap stops it
Two independent causes. The quality criterion is pole specific: the same surface as a band with the apex
cut away gives 406 triangles at maxDeflection 0.05 with the criterion on and 402 with it off. The
deflection cascade at 5e-5 is not pole specific - the band hits the cap just the same.
That defect does not corrupt the fingerprint below: ShellMetrics measures at size*1e-3 = 0.064, where the
face triangulates cleanly. It only costs the runtime, roughly 26 seconds per repeat.
